newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, led by petrochem shares.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, led by petrochem shares.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Monday, led by petrochemical shares, which soared on falling international naphtha prices, brokers said.
"Petrochemical shares were a main contributor to Monday's rise," said Lee Young-won, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
The composite stock index closed 7.25 points higher at 704.20. Brokers said today's rise was also fuelled by growing customer deposits with securities houses.
The deposits were estimated at 3.06 trillion won, compared with 3.04 trillion on Saturday, brokers said.
Volume totalled 43.25 million shares against 31.48 million for Saturday's half-day trading.
Gainers outpaced losers 505 to 283 with 114 unchanged.
Honam Petrochemical went limit-up, rising 1,000 won to 14,500, LG Chemical gained 300 won to 10,600.
Brokers said blue chips also rose as institutions, including investment trusts and insurers, went on a buying spree ahead of the planned expansion of the foreign stock ownership limit.
The limit will be raised to 23 percent on May 2 from the current 20 percent.

Bank shares rose slightly despite a media report that the finance ministry would oppose a recommendation by the presidential commission looking into financial reform to allow business conglomerates a say in bank management.
Buying of insurance stocks was backed by the commission's recommendation that business scope of financial institutions be expanded.
The commission submitted an 18-point report aimed at reforming the nation's backward financial industry to President Kim Young-sam.
